## Research and capabilities

- Primary research direction: program analysis and agent-enhanced security tools for vulnerability discovery and validation.
- Earlier work: static analysis of dynamic PHP behavior and unsafe data flows in CoBrA; scalable JavaScript analysis in FAST.
- Current work: agent-assisted analysis and fuzzing for business-rule violations, with runtime evidence checking findings; found 47 previously unknown logic vulnerabilities in PHP e-commerce applications; paper in progress.
- Planned exploration of agents for security: identify implicit business rules from application interfaces and observed interactions, then test which rule violations have security consequences; candidate rules require validation rather than being assumed to express security requirements.
- Additional research direction: security of agentic systems, including untrusted context, planning, tool use, cross-step state, task-constraint violations, and unauthorized outcomes; logic vulnerabilities in agentic workflows are an intended extension.
- Related studies: AnonVul concerns faithful evaluation of vulnerability-discovery agents; 3R-Bench concerns effects of conversational context on LLM cybersecurity assistance.
- Strengths: combines program-analysis research with system implementation; takes research from analysis design through implementation, debugging, and empirical evaluation; builds developer tools and contributes to established analysis software.
- Role fit: software-security research, program-analysis research, agentic-security research, and research engineering.
- Languages used across research and software contributions: Kotlin, Python, JavaScript, PHP, C++, Rust, Scala.

## Research contributions and publications

### CoBrA

- Research direction: Program analysis: dynamic PHP analysis.
- Title: CoBrA: Context-, Branch-sensitive Static Analysis for Detecting Taint-style Vulnerabilities in PHP Web Applications.
- Venue: ICSE 2026; status: published.
- Authors: Yichao Xu, Mingqing Kang, Neil Thimmaiah, Rigel Gjomemo, V. N. Venkatakrishnan, Yinzhi Cao.
- Contribution: first author and lead engineer; designed and built the Kotlin PHP static analyzer.
- Method: context- and branch-sensitive taint analysis; an abstract domain graph and stretch-relax algorithm resolve dynamic PHP behavior and track taint across functions.
- Results: 54 previously unknown vulnerabilities in 19 real-world applications; 9 assigned CVE identifiers, using the paper-reported count.
- Benchmark: 88.66% detection rate and below 0.3% false-positive rate on the PHP tarpits benchmark.
- Period: 2023-05–2025-03.
- Paper: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3744916.3773195
- PDF: https://www.yinzhicao.org/COBRA/cobra.pdf
- Code and datasets: https://github.com/jhu-seclab-cobra

### FAST

- Research direction: Program analysis: scalable JavaScript analysis.
- Title: Scaling JavaScript Abstract Interpretation to Detect and Exploit Node.js Taint-style Vulnerability.
- Venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy 2023; status: published.
- Authors: Mingqing Kang, Yichao Xu, Song Li, Rigel Gjomemo, Jianwei Hou, V. N. Venkatakrishnan, Yinzhi Cao.
- Contribution: second author; implemented JavaScript abstract interpretation and led evaluation, including reproducing 4 prior analyzers and building comparison and debugging utilities.
- Method: bottom-up abstract interpretation resolves dynamic calls; top-down interpretation prunes unrelated statements and checks path constraints for exploitability.
- Study results: 242 previously unknown vulnerabilities in npm packages; 21 assigned CVE identifiers.
- Period: 2021-05–2022-11.
- Paper: https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10179352
- PDF: https://www.yinzhicao.org/FAST/ODGen-FAST.pdf
- Code: https://github.com/fast-sp-2023/fast

### AnonVul

- Research direction: Agent-enhanced security tools: evaluating vulnerability-discovery agents.
- Title: Discovery or Memorization? A Faithful Benchmark for Real-World Business-Logic Vulnerability Discovery.
- Status: arXiv preprint, 2026.
- Authors: Rui Yang, Yichao Xu, Zhuohao Zhang, Jiahao Ji, Chaowei Xiao, Yinzhi Cao, Ziyang Li.
- Contribution: co-author, second in the author list.
- Study: evaluates discovery versus memorization using anonymized business-logic vulnerability tasks, sandboxed execution, and expert-specified success checks.
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.17542
- PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.17542

### 3R-Bench

- Research direction: Agentic security: context and cybersecurity assistance.
- Title: Same Request, Different Boundary: Evaluating Cybersecurity Assistance across Conversational Contexts.
- Status: arXiv preprint, 2026.
- Authors: Rui Yang, Yang Hong, Yichao Xu, Zhengyu Liu, Yinzhi Cao, Ziyang Li.
- Contribution: co-author.
- Study: measures how conversational history changes responses to identical cybersecurity requests; distinguishes refusal, bounded assistance, compliance, and provider blocking.
- Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00578
- PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.00578

### Earlier publication

- Title: A Denial of Services Attack for IOT System.
- Venue: Science and Wealth, 2018-06; ISSN 1671-2226.
